description: Fix the payment acknowledgment email so every leading emoji/icon renders inline with (or centered above) its text instead of detaching to the far-left edge, at both desktop and narrow/mobile widths. Scope is strictly the email template markup/styles in src/components/dashboard/new-booking-dialog.tsx (buildPaymentAckEmailHtml) and the shared signature block in src/lib/email-signature.ts (buildEmailSignature). Do NOT touch booking form logic, save flow, bulk/draft, or profit/GST calculations. ROOT CAUSE: the emoji are HTML-entity emoji (not ). They detach to the left because (1) the @media (max-width:640px) rule `.stack, .grid-2 td, .grid-3 td, .grid-4 td { display:block !important; width:100% !important }` converts table cells that rely on the `align="center"` HTML attribute into block elements that no longer honor `align`, so their content (including the leading emoji) left-aligns; and (2) several blocks that lead with an emoji have no explicit text-align, so when a client applies emoji font substitution / the block is not centered by an ancestor, the leading glyph anchors to the left line-box start. The email-safe fix is to (a) add an explicit `text-align:center` fallback to the stacked cells in the media query, and (b) ensure every block/cell whose content leads with an emoji carries an explicit inline `text-align:center` (matching where the section already centers) so the icon can never detach to the left when the layout stacks. Do NOT alter the hero LOGO (display:block;margin:0 auto is intentional) or the footer social icons.
steps: Read src/components/dashboard/new-booking-dialog.tsx lines ~226-518 (the buildPaymentAckEmailHtml template literal) and src/lib/email-signature.ts in full before editing.

In the <style> block media query (~line 246) update the stacked-cell rule so stacked cells re-center their content. Change `.stack, .grid-2 td, .grid-3 td, .grid-4 td { display:block !important; width:100% !important; box-sizing:border-box !important; padding:6px 0 !important; }` to ALSO include `text-align:center !important;`. This is the primary fix: when cells stop being table-cells (losing the align="center" attribute) they keep centered content. Verify this does not visually harm the two-column left-aligned card blocks (Plan / Tenure / Location / Activation grid-2, and the footer 55/45 grid) — those card contents (title + description) reading centered when stacked on mobile is acceptable and matches the flagged fix intent; keep them centered for consistency.

Trust-stats row (~lines 296-318, the 5,000+/4.9 star/97%/48 hrs block): the <td class="stack" align="center"> already sets align center; the emoji is inside `4.9 ★` within a centered div. Add explicit `text-align:center` to each stat's inner <div> wrappers if not already centered by the parent <td style>. Ensure the star stays with 4.9 by keeping them in the same inline run (they already are). Confirm no change needed to numbers.

Green banner emoji line (~line 291, `🎉 You're now part of the family of 5,000+ growing brands`): the containing <div> has no text-align. Add `text-align:center;` to that green banner div's inline style so the party emoji sits inline centered with the text and never anchors left when stacked.

'Hello <name>' line (~line 285, `Hello ${client_name} 👋`): its parent <td> already has text-align:center, and the div is centered — verify the waving-hand emoji stays inline with the name (it is in the same inline run). Add text-align:center to the specific div if it is missing so it is robust.

Confidential/trust line in dark welcome section (~line 466, `🔒 Payment secured · 💼 Compliance-first · ⭐ 4.9/5 rated`): the <div> has no text-align but its ancestor <td> is text-align:center. Add explicit `text-align:center;` to this div's inline style so the lock/briefcase/star emoji cannot detach when the client renders them.
Top eyebrow line (~line 267, `🔒 Payment Acknowledgment · Officially Confirmed`): its <td> already has text-align:center — confirm robust; no change needed unless emoji still could detach.

'YOUR DEDICATED MANAGER' block in src/lib/email-signature.ts: the eyebrow `
👨‍💼 Your Dedicated Manager
` sits in a card whose outer div is text-align:center, so it should be centered — but add explicit text-align:center to that eyebrow div and to any emoji-leading div (the CALL DIRECT `📞` and EMAIL ME `✉` icon divs inside the grid-2 stacked cells) so that when the grid-2 cells stack to display:block on mobile, the phone/envelope icons stay centered above their labels rather than detaching left. The grid-2 stacked cells contain blocks whose inner icon divs must read text-align:center (the parent is display:block); add text-align:center to the or the icon div.

For each PAYMENT SUMMARY / SERVICE DETAILS / NEXT STEPS card that leads with an emoji inside a left-aligned card (e.g. `📦 Plan`, `📅 Tenure`, `📍 Location(s) Covered`, `⚡ Activation Window`, `📄 Document Verification`, etc.): these emoji lead inline text runs `
📦 Plan
`. They are inside cards that are intentionally left-aligned (grid-2) or center (grid-3 next-steps). Do NOT force these to center if the card is intentionally left-aligned at desktop; the reported bug is the icon detaching to a SEPARATE far-left position, which is the stacking/align issue fixed in step 2. Confirm these emoji remain in the same inline run as their label (they already are) so they never separate from the text. No structural change needed beyond the media-query centering fix unless inspection shows a wrapping element splitting icon from label.

The two summary-table rows with leading emoji in a <td> (`💰 Amount Paid`, `⚠️ Balance Remaining`): these are normal left-aligned table cells with the emoji inline before the label text — they are fine and should stay left-aligned inline. Confirm no change needed.

Do a final pass over the whole template + signature confirming: (a) every emoji that leads a CENTERED section's block has explicit text-align:center on its block, (b) the media query stacked-cell rule now includes text-align:center, (c) the LOGO (display:block;margin:0 auto) and footer social are untouched, (d) no booking form logic, save flow, GST/profit calc, or bulk/draft code was modified.

Stage and commit ONLY src/components/dashboard/new-booking-dialog.tsx and src/lib/email-signature.ts with a clear conventional-commit message like `fix(email): keep payment-ack icons inline/centered with their text (stop left-edge detach)`. Do NOT push or open a PR.
acceptance_criteria: The @media (max-width:640px) stacked-cell rule in new-booking-dialog.tsx includes `text-align:center !important;` so stacked grid/stat cells re-center content after losing the align attribute.
The green 'family of 5,000+' banner div, the dark-section 'Payment secured / Compliance-first / 4.9/5 rated' div, and the 'Hello <name>' div each carry an explicit inline text-align:center.

In email-signature.ts, the 'Your Dedicated Manager' eyebrow div and the CALL DIRECT / EMAIL ME icon blocks inside the grid-2 stacked cells are explicitly centered so their phone/envelope emoji stay above their labels when stacked.
The hero LOGO (display:block; margin:0 auto) and the footer social-icon tags are unchanged.
No changes outside the two email-template files; no booking form logic, save flow, bulk/draft, or GST/profit-calc code is modified (git diff shows only the email markup/style lines).
Every leading emoji remains in the same inline text run as its label (icon never sits in a separate element that could detach).
verification: git diff origin/main --stat shows only src/components/dashboard/new-booking-dialog.tsx and src/lib/email-signature.ts changed.
Inspect git diff to confirm the media-query text-align:center addition and per-section text-align:center additions are present and no booking logic lines changed.

Cannot run `bun run build` / `npx tsc --noEmit` in sandbox (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY, npm 403). CI will run both on PR. Note this limitation in findings and confirm the change is pure string/markup with no TS syntax risk (edits are inside a template literal / returned string).
Grep the template to confirm text-align:center appears on the flagged blocks and the media query.
